paper.title: Earmarked paternity leave and the relative income within couples
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement and no Statistics Denmark project reference is given. …

registers.name_in_paper: linked longitudinal administrative Danish register data on the universe of individuals in Denmark
registers.role: sample frame / treatment / outcomes / controls / linkage
outcomes (number of days of leave of the mother and the father; annual amount of leave benefits)
outcomes (annual labor income of each household member, used to build the woman’s labor income share)

linkages: Women are linked to their first child and to the partner they were married to or cohabiting with at the time of birth (the ‘birth-partner’); only years in which the woman is registered as partner with the birth-partner are used
Household members are linked so that household labor income can be split into the woman’s and the man’s annual labor income
Each household member is linked to their sector of employment (public or private) one year prior to the first childbirth

sample.universe: The universe of individuals in Denmark, 1980 to 2013
selection_rules: Women aged 20 to 60 who give birth to their first child during 1995 through 2001 (a narrow window around the 1998 reform, because the maternity leave system was also reformed in 1994 and 2002)
The woman was either married or cohabiting at the time of birth; the partner at the time of birth is the ‘birth-partner’
Opposite-sex couples with at most 15 years of age difference
Only years in which the woman is registered as partner with the birth-partner are used
Years in which either household member is registered as predominantly studying, outside the labor market, or with negative labor income are dropped
The period from 3 years prior to the first birth to 8 years after the first birth
sample.period: Register data 1980-2013; first births 1995-2001; event window -3 to +8 years around the first birth

construction_notes: The primary variable is the share of household labor income earned by the woman, based on the total annual labor income for each household member

Annual variables are used because labor income and received parental leave benefits are available annually from Statistics Denmark
Birth-month dummies are included for the year of birth and for the year after childbirth because of substantial seasonality in the annual labor income share

Summary statistics (Table A1 in the Supplemental Material, described on p. 86): the woman’s labor income share drops from around 42% to around 32% at childbirth and increases to around 39% after eight years

claims.statement: The 1998 Danish reform, which increased earmarked paternity leave for fathers from two to four weeks, increased the woman’s share of household labor income.

treatment.label: Treatment T_{i,t}: first child born after the 1998 earmarked paternity leave reform

definition.value: T_{i,t} = FirstChildAfter1998Reform_{i,t} · 1(YearsSinceFirstBirth_{i,t} ≥ 0): equals one when a child born after the reform is present in the household and is zero otherwise. The April 1998 reform entitled all fathers of children born after October 15, 1997 to two additional earmarked weeks of paternity leave (two to four weeks in total), to be taken in weeks 25 and 26 after childbirth; all remaining features of the leave system were unchanged.

timing.value: Switches on from the year of the first birth onwards (years since first birth ≥ 0) for couples whose first child was born on or after October 15, 1997. Identification compares first births within one year before the reform (control) with first births within one year after the reform (treated).
